title: C412 — Left-hand rear lamp assembly connector
introduction:
I use this page as the address book for the left-hand rear lamp connection. The drawing tells you where a cavity label sits; the table tells you what that address belongs to. A circle in the housing drawing is not, by itself, a promise that a circuit lives there.

Begin with the connector identification, then match an illustrated label to its Cavity row. Read across for the circuit, color, gauge, function and terminal reference. Keep each function’s side wording exactly as printed, including the signal-out description that names the opposite side. That wording alone does not explain the signal’s route or justify relabeling it. The pigtail listing is a separate parts cross-reference.

This is a connector-reading guide. Physical viewing direction, access, release movements, probing conditions and replacement steps require other information. The sheet also leaves the gauge convention and Size and Used codes undefined; preserve those fields without assigning extra meanings to them.

edits.why: The drawing has a broad projection on the left, smaller projections on the right and a hooked outline at the lower right. I use those features to keep the page layout straight while reading the cavity labels. The shaded lower-left cavity corresponds to the table row with blank circuit and function fields. Its position remains part of the housing map, without supplying a circuit assignment.

Read from the illustrated cavity label into the matching table row, keeping the park, turn, ground, signal-out and stop descriptions distinct. Circuit Number identifies the circuit; Color and Gauge describe its listed wire, and Terminal Part Number is its terminal reference. I leave the blank row blank and retain the opposite-side signal-out wording. Neither is a reason to invent a missing connection or a fault conclusion.

The pigtail is the connector-and-wire-lead service item. Match Kit List to Number and compare Hard Shell with Engineering Shell to follow the references between tables. Service Part belongs to that listed item, whereas the pin table identifies individual terminals. The pigtail Gauge field does not authorize substituting that gauge for each circuit wire, and this listing does not teach a splice or replacement procedure.
